newsitem.title: MEXICO: HSBC James Capel raises Mexico growth forecast.
newsitem.headline: HSBC James Capel raises Mexico growth forecast.

text.p: HSBC James Capel has raised its forecast of second quarter gross domestic product growth in Mexico to 5.5 percent from "near" 4.0 percent, the brokerage said in a statement Wednesday.

Because of the change, James Capel economist Gray Newman raised his full-year Mexico GDP forecast to 4.4 percent from a range of 3.5-4.0 percent. He lowered his year-end peso forecast to 8.45 per dollar from 8.9.

"After warning investors for nearly a year and a half not to overestimate the strength of consumer spending, we are now faced with a case for a much hardier picture of consumer demand," Newman said in the report.
A stronger peso goes hand-in-hand with a stronger economic growth forecast, the report said.
Newman said the reasons for stronger growth in the second quarter were:
- strong April industrial production and manufacturing reports;
- a healthy May survey of manufacturing opinion;
- a consumption pickup in April and May retail reports;
- significant overshooting of 1997 monetary base targets. But Newman said some of the pickup could be temporary.
"Despite our optimism for good growth during 1997, we have decided against raising our full-year GDP forecast as much as our models suggest," he said.

"While we believe conditions are ripe for some improvement in consumer spending, the timing of the current recovery in consumption -- just months before key mid-term elections -- raises the specter that part of the improvement may be tied to election spending or even election fears."
